chapter_title: Chương 59: 0059【Tuyển Tập Văn Mẫu Cũng Có Hàng Nhái】

segments.title: Chương 59: 0059【Tuyển Tập Văn Mẫu Cũng Có Hàng Nhái】
segments.content:
"Classmate, what's your name?"

As soon as the proctor collected the essay, a contestant couldn't help but ask.

Another contestant also came over: "What did you write? The two proctors were standing next to you the whole time, watching."

In the blink of an eye, Chen Guiliang was surrounded.

Milan and Luo Jin, who had come with him on the train, silently walked to the door of the examination room.

There were too many people around Chen Guiliang, and they couldn't be bothered to squeeze through.

"Chen Guiliang will definitely get a first prize, right?" Luo Jin said.

Milan nodded: "The proctors stood there for so long. His writing is probably more than just good, so good it was like peeking into a different world."

Luo Jin mumbled: "There are only about twenty spots for the first prize in Group A. Now there's one less."

"What are you guys talking about?"

Chen Xiaoping walked over from the next examination room, followed by Lei Yujie and Li Zhen. The three of them were from Dafoshi and stuck together all the time.

Luo Jin pointed inside: "Chen Guiliang is surrounded."

"What happened to him?" Lei Yujie asked.

Milan explained: "Halfway through the exam, two proctors just stood next to Chen Guiliang without moving, watching him write his essay. When they collected the papers, they even put Chen Guiliang's essay on the very top."

"I'm afraid he's getting a first prize!" Lei Yujie exclaimed.

A girl who had followed them over asked: "Who is Chen Guiliang?"

"Chen Guiliang is also a contestant from our Sichuan," Chen Xiaoping briefly explained, then made an introduction. "This is Chen Xueyuan, from Chengdu Foreign Languages School. Chen Xueyuan, these two are Milan and Luo Jin."

"Hello!"

"Hello!"

Both Milan and Luo Jin sized up Chen Xueyuan.

Her Chengdu Foreign Languages School was already quite famous in Sichuan—an aristocratic school, the alma mater of Harvard girl Liu Yiting.

It seems she even published a book, but it's all fluff and no substance. For students at an aristocratic school, having a cell phone was normal. Chen Xueyuan dialed a number and said, "Hello, is everyone here? Come over once you're all together. I'm outside the Group A examination hall."

In an instant, seven or eight contestants from Group B arrived, all first and second-year students from the foreign languages school.

The total number of registered contestants in Group A was 200, with 199 present.

The total number of registered contestants in Group B was 200, with 196 present.

Among the 395 contestants present, a full 39 were from Sichuan.

There were also many contestants from Shandong, Hunan, Henan, Hubei, and Zhejiang.

Especially Shandong, which was second only to Sichuan.

"When is he going to come out?" Milan glanced into the examination room again and saw that the crowd around Chen Guiliang was growing.

It was unclear how the news spread, but it became more and more exaggerated, claiming Chen Guiliang was pre-selected for the first prize.

Even the contestants in the neighboring few examination rooms had heard about it.

Chen Guiliang was speechless and could only shout: "I chose the second topic! I used a small bird to symbolize the benevolent and noble people throughout Chinese history. The tree branch symbolizes the resilient spirit of Chinese civilization. The wind and waves of the sea symbolize the countless calamities China has faced over thousands of years."

"What a profound theme. How come I didn't think of that?"

"It's nothing special."

"What you're saying isn't very specific. Did you use that 'peeking into another world' style of writing?"

"Classmate, what's your QQ number? We can discuss literature on QQ."

"..."

Chen Guiliang pushed his way out. "Excuse me, please let me through."

After escaping the scene in a fluster, Chen Guiliang saw Milan and the others. He quickened his pace and said, "I'm going back to the hotel first!"

It was already 11:30 in the morning.

When the contestants checked into the hotel, they had already booked set meals.

Fearing he would be pestered again, Chen Guiliang took his food back to his room to eat, then sat by the window listening to music and dozing off.

Before long, the five contestants he had met on the train all finished their lunch and came running over to get the latest news.

The girl named Chen Xueyuan also tagged along.

"I asked around when I was eating downstairs just now. Eight out of ten people chose the first topic, and the central themes of their essays were pretty much the same," said Lei Yujie.

Chen Xiaoping looked dejected: "I also chose the first topic. I'm afraid my chances are slim."

Milan asked: "Chen Guiliang, what did you actually write? Be more specific."

The others all cast curious gazes at him.

Chen Guiliang said: "I wrote a poem, and then I wrote a preface for the poem."

Luo Jin exclaimed in amazement: "You're so bold, daring to write a poem in a writing competition! No wonder the proctors stood there watching you."

They all assumed it was a modern poem, so they didn't press him further.

Chen Xueyuan suggested: "Why don't we go to the Bund? And what about Huaihai Road and Jinling Road?"

Li Zhen asked: "Are those two roads far from the Bund?"

"I don't know." Chen Xueyuan shook her head.

Milan said: "Forget it. It just started raining again. It won't be much fun to go shopping."

"Knock, knock, knock!"

As they were chatting, a knock suddenly came at the door.

Luo Jin went to open it. Standing outside was a middle-aged man in a suit.

He thought it was a staff member from the New Concept competition and quickly bowed. "Hello, teacher. May I help you?"

"My surname is Han, an editor from Petroleum Publishing House."

Seeing that there were six or seven people in the room, the middle-aged man was very pleased and quickly took out a stack of business cards to hand out.

Lei Yujie looked at the card and said, "What does a publishing house want with us?"

This Editor Han said: "It's like this. Our publishing house is planning to publish a collection of works by the winners of the New Concept competition. As long as it's a manuscript from a winner of this year's competition, we'll accept it. The remuneration is very considerable!"

Milan carefully examined the information on the card and asked suspiciously, "I've bought the collection of winning works from the New Concept competition for three years in a row. It seems you're not the publisher, are you?"

Editor Han explained with a smile: "We publish a collection of the winners' works, not the winning works."

Winners' works.

Winning works.

The difference of a single word changed the meaning.

The group mulled it over, not knowing whether to laugh or cry.

Editor Han elaborated: "The organizers of the New Concept competition only own the publishing rights to your preliminary and final round essays. You are completely free to use your other articles to earn manuscript fees. For first prize articles, it's 200 yuan per thousand characters. For second prize articles, it's 150 yuan per thousand characters. For third prize articles, it's 80 yuan per thousand characters."

When the prices were announced, everyone except Chen Guiliang was tempted.

Although Chen Xueyuan, who studied at an aristocratic school, never lacked pocket money, earning her own manuscript fees was different.

Chen Xueyuan quickly asked: "Do we have to submit the manuscript before leaving the Magic City? Do we also need to sign a contract?"

Editor Han said: "You can submit it anytime before May. Of course, we also need to review the manuscripts; we won't accept something just written casually. If any of you have good articles, you can send them to our publishing house at any time. We are a legitimate company. You can look us up if you don't believe me."

It was indeed legitimate, and everything was legal.

But every year, they thoroughly disgusted the New Concept organizers and their partner publishing house.

The organizers published *The Collection of Award-Winning Works from the Xth National New Concept Writing Competition*, a title that was seventeen characters long.

And the counterfeit version?

They simply added the character for "person" or "-er" ("者") to the title, changing "Award-Winning Works" to "Award-Winners' Works."

It was extremely hard to tell the difference, but it wasn't illegal.

When students or parents went to buy the book, they intended to buy the real Li Kui, but with a moment of carelessness, they ended up with the fake Li Gui.

"I won't disturb you any longer. Goodbye!"

Editor Han quickly took his leave and went to knock on the next door.

Luo Jin stuck his head out for a look, then closed the door again, saying gleefully: "I can't believe there's such a good deal. One or two hundred yuan per thousand characters! I can earn one or two thousand if I write ten thousand characters!"

Chen Xueyuan said: "I want to start writing right now and spend the manuscript fees I earn myself!"

"You all think you're going to win an award?" Chen Xiaoping said with a smile.

Milan said: "At the very least, it'll be a third prize. It would be too embarrassing to only get an honorable mention."

About ten minutes later, an editor from another magazine came knocking.

It seemed the "Li Guis" were also competing with each other.

This time, the remuneration offered was 20 yuan per thousand characters higher than the previous one across the board.

The kids in the room instantly forgot all about Editor Han.

They were both excited about earning manuscript fees and anxious about the competition results.

They finally made it to dinner time. The group went downstairs to eat together, then returned to their respective rooms to wait for a phone call.

Luo Jin wished he could hug the landline phone!

He waited anxiously for a long time, then turned his head to see Chen Guiliang writing something. He couldn't help but laugh, "Eager to earn manuscript fees already?"

"I'm bored," Chen Guiliang said.

Luo Jin abandoned the landline and walked over, wanting to see Chen Guiliang's article. He only glanced at it before exclaiming, "Holy shit! You're actually doing a test paper? You even brought your math book! Dude, we're here for a writing competition. Why are you doing math problems?"

Chen Guiliang said: "To pass the time."

He wasn't lying. He was genuinely bored.

Without a smartphone, he could only watch TV shows, which was worse than doing math papers.

During the train ride two days ago, Chen Guiliang had often lain in his soft sleeper reading a math book.

"You're incredible. Absolutely amazing!"

Luo Jin gave him a thumbs-up, it was hard to tell if it was praise or sarcasm.

For the next fifty-something minutes, one guarded the landline while the other did his test paper.

"Ring ring ring ring~~~"

The landline rang.

Luo Jin felt as if he'd been electrocuted. His right hand shot out, snatched the receiver, and he said, "Hello, this is Luo Jin."

A voice came from the phone: "This is Mengya's Editor-in-Chief Zhao Changtian. Is Chen Guiliang in the room?"

"Yes, he is," Luo Jin replied.

Zhao Changtian said: "The two of you, come over together to meet the teachers from the major universities."

Luo Jin's whole body trembled slightly with excitement. "Editor-in-Chief Zhao, did we win an award?"

"Yes, both first prizes," Zhao Changtian said. "The official awards ceremony is tomorrow. Tonight, you'll communicate with the admissions officers first."

"Thank you, Editor-in-Chief Zhao. Thank you!" Luo Jin thanked him profusely.

He hung up the phone and began to jump up and down in the room.

After letting off some steam, Luo Jin ran over and closed Chen Guiliang's book and papers. "What's the point of doing math papers? We both won awards, and they're both first prizes!"

Chen Guiliang was slightly surprised.

He was surprised that his temporary roommate had also won a first prize.

The two of them left the hotel room together. They had only walked a few steps down the corridor when they saw Milan also coming out of her room.

"You guys won?" Milan said, pleasantly surprised.

Luo Jin asked: "What prize did you get?"

Milan said: "First prize."

Chen Guiliang said: "..."

In the hotel rooms on this floor, people were constantly coming out into the corridor.

All of them were first prize winners.

Chen Guiliang even saw Li Zhen from Dafoshi.

This time, among the contestants from Sichuan, there were four Group A first prize winners and four Group B first prize winners.

It was quite ridiculous.

Everyone congratulated each other, talking and laughing as they headed to the main hall upstairs.

Li Zhen said: "It seems each university has a limited number of spots. We can coordinate so we don't end up competing against each other."

"I've also asked around," Luo Jin said. "In the past few years of the New Concept competition, Fudan and Beijing Normal University have offered the most spots. The terms from Nanjing University, Xiamen University, and East China Normal University are also very good!"

Milan said: "I'm applying to Fudan!"

"My grades aren't that good. I'll apply to Beijing Normal," Luo Jin said.

Li Zhen said: "Then I'll choose East China Normal."

"What about Chen Guiliang?"

The three of them looked at Chen Guiliang.

Chen Guiliang didn't know yet; he wanted to see what each school had to offer first.

Suddenly, a staff member shouted: "Group A, go to the left. Group B, go to the right."

Group B consisted of first and second-year high school students and a few middle school students. They were naturally not there to discuss university admission, but mainly to inquire about summer camps, winter camps, and other related information.

For example, Tsinghua's winter camp was willing to give spots to New Concept's Group B.

If this was handled well, it was also possible to take a shortcut to get into Tsinghua.

Why did aristocratic schools like Chengdu Foreign Languages have so many first and second-year students flocking to the competition?

They were aiming for the winter and summer camps!

It was possible that just by singing a song at a winter camp, they could get a direct recommendation to Tsinghua.

"Chen Guiliang, come over here."

Hu Weishi was waving at him from a distance.

The writers had gone out to party tonight; those present were all professors from major universities.

More than one key university had prepared excellent admission terms for Chen Guiliang!

Some schools hadn't secured their admission quotas yet, but that didn't stop them from trying to sweet-talk him first.

(The situation with this year's first prizes was indeed ridiculous. Sichuan, Zhejiang, and the Imperial Capital tied for first place in the number of winners. The first prize winners from these three places directly accounted for 40% of the total.)
